title: Read back before acting: acting is changing something; reading is reconstitution itself
situation: The operator observed that at session start an agent first orients on its instructions and the operator's prompt, so 'read the design back first' cannot mean the session's first output, and a judge or gate reading it that way misses its intent. The readback gate has refused acts very often (28 refusals in 4 runs of one example), consistent with holding the reads that produce the readback, or the reply that answers the prompt.
decision: Reconstitution's 'before acting' orders the readback before any change, never before anything at all. Acting is changing something: recording or accepting in the journal, dispatching, editing or committing work, approving an example. Orienting on instructions and the prompt, and reading the context overview, the journal and the ledger, are reconstitution itself and are never held. The readback is given in the first reply that carries substance, and may be that reply's answer to the operator's prompt; a session whose prompt asks only where things stand has given its readback by answering. Judges and gates judge only the readback's order relative to changes.
consequences: The readback gate holds only changing acts until the readback is given, and lets every read through; the readback rubrics judge order against changes only.
